decisions.quote: In the present research, we examined the prevalence of Gettier intuitions in counterfeit-object Gettier-type cases by replicating and extending Experiment 1 of Turri et al. (2015).
decisions.location: Discussion, line 239 (see also Title, line 9, and References, line 374)
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly replicates Experiment 1 of Turri, Buckwalter, & Blouw (2015), cited in the reference list (line 374) as 'Turri, J., Buckwalter, W., & Blouw, P. (2015). Knowledge and luck. Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, 22(2), 378–390. https://doi.org/10.3758/s13423-014-0683-5'. The shipped row misidentified the target as a single-author SSRN paper ('Knowledge and Assertion in Gettier Cases', 10.2139/ssrn.3649814) that is not in the reference list.

decisions.quote: This result did not correspond to that found by Turri et al., who failed to detect a significant difference in knowledge attribution between these two conditions. Notably, the size of the Gettier intuition effect varied by vignette in our research; the Darrel vignette from the original study produced the smallest effect size and was similar to that we calculated using the non-significant result from the Turri et al. Therefore, we do find effect sizes in the same range as Turri et al. when directly comparing like conditions; however, the null result did not replicate.
decisions.location: Discussion, line 239 (see also lines 241-242 and Conclusion, line 280)
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind code 'failed'. Resolving the dependent original identity to Turri, Buckwalter, & Blouw (2015) Experiment 1 confirms this outcome: whereas Turri et al. (2015) reported a null difference in knowledge attributions between the counterfeit-object Gettier ('Threat') condition and the matched justified true belief ('No Threat' knowledge control) condition, this replication found significantly higher knowledge attribution in the knowledge control condition than in the Gettier condition both overall and in the original Darrel vignette, and the authors explicitly conclude that the original null result did not replicate and that their findings contradict Turri et al.'s conclusion.

decisions.quote: In a large-scale, cross-cultural conceptual replication of Turri and colleagues’ (2015) Experiment 1 (N = 4,724) using a within-participants design and three vignettes across 19 geopolitical regions, we did find evidence for Gettier intuitions; participants were 1.86 times more likely to attribute knowledge to protagonists in standard cases of justified true belief than to protagonists in Gettier-type cases.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind rightly classify this study as a replication: it collected new cross-cultural multi-site data to re-test the empirical finding of Experiment 1 of Turri, Buckwalter, & Blouw (2015).
